The last word in podcasting news.

Every Friday, James Cridland and Sam Sethi review the week's top stories from Podnews; and interview some of the biggest names making the news from across the podcast industry.

item.description:
Send James and Sam a message or voicemail

Sam gets out of his sick bed and joins James for a discussion of the latest podcast industry news.

• iHeartMedia sale rumours versus a financial reporting split for investors 
• Radio’s share of listening in the UK, US, and Canada versus podcasting’s smaller base 
• Duplicate podcast feeds and hosting accountability through an industry code of practice 
• Meta-hosted AI podcast production at scale and the risks of unpoliced synthetic content 
• Spoofed user agents, broken analytics, and Common Access Tokens as a practical signal 
• Podcast ad load growth, listener tolerance, and how it compares with radio ad minutes 
• AI-assisted video repackaging for YouTube and LinkedIn and what actually moves numbers 
• Unified creator dashboards, why downloads persist, and the missing “plays” debate 
• Membership bundles, newsletters, and using the Podcasting 2.0 funding tag for paid offers 
• Webby credits registry as an IMDB-like ledger for podcast and digital work 
• Industry moves including SiriusXM’s new CEO and the collapse of Message Heard 
• HLS video support, “video-first” marketing confusion, and why RSS video still matters

item.description:
Send James and Sam a message or voicemail

We dig into how podcast theft actually works, why one-click importing and monetization can turn into an engine for piracy, and what hosting platforms should change right now. We also look at where the creator economy is heading as newsletters, subscriptions, AI tools, and algorithmic discovery reshape how people find and fund audio.
• Spreaker’s import and monetisation flow enabling cloned podcasts and chart manipulation
• RSS.com handling of a hijacked show including ad revenue repayment and feed recovery
• PodProtect and the need for detection plus a hosting code of conduct
• Newsletter and membership convergence with Supercast adding newsletters
• Beehive’s monetisation suite including dynamic ad insertion, targeting, and ad-free subscriptions
• Instagram testing 90-minute horizontal video and what it means for podcasters
• Kate Cocker’s 3,000 consecutive daily episodes and how community drives content
• The business reality of ads in short-form daily podcasts and listener expectations
• The shift from followers to algorithms plus new discovery-first podcast apps
• Spotify’s AI agent questions, subscription risk, and the subscription model trend
• Progress on transcripts accessibility as SiriusXM lawsuit nears settlement
• Tooling updates including Buzzsprout’s admin app and Riverside’s AI agents
